title: Customer 360 business view serves unmasked phone, email and full home address to an associate that the subscription-customers surface masks for the same identity
actor: STAFF role_code=associate (assoc@pawspace.test), permissions include customers.view but NOT customers.view_full_phone
request:
Two GETs with the same headers {oai-authenticated-user-email: assoc@pawspace.test, oai-authenticated-user-full-name: Probe%20User, oai-authenticated-user-full-name-encoding: percent-encoded-utf-8}:
(a) GET https://uat.pawspace.in/api/subscription-customers
(b) GET https://uat.pawspace.in/api/customer-360?customerId=CUST-1
Gateway check first: authorizeApiRequest(GET /api/customer-360, {DB}) -> {"denied":false,"actor":{"email":"assoc@pawspace.test","roleCode":"associate","permissions":["dashboard.view","customers.view","bookings.view","scheduling.book","pricing.view","communications.call","communications.message","communications.manage","attendance.view","leave.view","performance.view","self_service.view"],"preview":false},"permission":"customers.view"} (ALLOW)
d1_before: app_users: ('USR-ASSOC','assoc@pawspace.test','Assoc','associate','active'); canonical_customers: ('CUST-1','Ritu Malhotra','+919876543210','ritu@example.com','blr'); customer_addresses: ('ADDR-1','CUST-1','Home','44 Victim Lane','Apt 3','Indiranagar','Bengaluru','560038',1); subscription_customers: ('CUST-1','Ritu Malhotra','+919876543210',...)
d1_after: unchanged (both reads are GET, cache-control:no-store, no writes; SELECT COUNT(*) on canonical_customers, customer_addresses and subscription_customers identical before and after)
repeatable: yes - identical output on two consecutive passes in the same process (pass 1 and pass 2 printed byte-identical bodies)
canonical_failure: lib/customer-360.ts line 45, in the record projection of buildCustomer360: `primaryPhone:String(base.primary_phone||'')` (and `email:base.email?String(base.email):null`, and the `addresses:addresses.map(...)` projection on the same line). buildCustomer360 takes no actor and never consults hasPermission(actor.permissions,"customers.view_full_phone"); app/api/customer-360/route.ts line 8 gates only on `authorize(request,"customers.view")` and passes no actor down. The platform's own convention is app/api/subscription-customers/route.ts line 42 `const reveal=hasPermission(actor.permissions,"customers.view_full_phone")` followed by maskPhone/maskName - customers.view_full_phone exists in the permission catalogue and is held only by admin/founder/superuser, so 'permission absent' is being treated as 'reveal allowed'.
money_consequence: No direct rupee misstatement. The exposure is contactable customer PII: for every customer in the CRM (buildCustomer360 reads up to 500 crm_contacts + 500 canonical_customers with no per-actor scoping), an associate obtains the full mobile number, email and street address. That is the exact dataset an associate would need to poach or resell a book of customers, and it defeats the masking control the platform already paid for on the sibling surface.
blast_radius: Every associate identity, every customer record on the platform (unscoped list when customerId is omitted). Reached through GET /api/customer-360 and, via the same buildCustomer360 call, GET /api/customer-business-view (customers.view).

title: Unit Economics counts refunds only at status='processed', a state the governed ops refund workflow never reaches - a fully completed Rs 5,000 refund is reported as refunds 0 and 100% contribution margin
actor: STAFF role_code=founder (admin@pawspace.test) driving the real POST /api/booking-operations refund workflow, then STAFF reading GET /api/unit-economics
request:
1) POST https://uat.pawspace.in/api/booking-operations {"bookingId":"BKG-1","providerId":"PRV-1","action":"refund_requested","reason":"Service not delivered"} -> 201 {"data":{...,"refundCaseId":"c412c378-c29e-4deb-b046-75d474a66528"}}
2) POST .../booking-operations {"action":"refund_status","refundCaseId":"c412c378-...","refundStatus":"approved",...} -> 200
3) same with "processing" -> 200
4) same with "completed" -> 200   (this is the terminal state the route's own transition map allows: {requested:[approved,rejected],approved:[processing],processing:[completed]})
5) GET https://uat.pawspace.in/api/unit-economics?from=2026-08-01&to=2026-08-31 (headers oai-authenticated-user-email: admin@pawspace.test)
d1_after:
SELECT id,booking_id,amount,status,approved_by FROM booking_refund_cases ->
[{"id":"c412c378-c29e-4deb-b046-75d474a66528","booking_id":"BKG-1","amount":5000,"status":"completed","approved_by":"PRV-1"}]
The money is gone from the business and the row says so; the report does not.
repeatable: yes - two independent worlds built and driven in the same process (pass1 and pass2), both produced refunds:0 / contributionKnown:5000 with a booking_refund_cases row at status='completed'
canonical_failure: lib/unit-economics.ts line 61: `const refunds=await chunkedIn(ids,(chunk,placeholders)=>safeAll(db,["booking_refund_cases"],`SELECT booking_id,amount FROM booking_refund_cases WHERE status='processed' AND booking_id IN (${placeholders})`,chunk,guards));`. The literal 'processed' is written ONLY by lib/grooming-payment-reconciliation.ts line 294 (the Razorpay refund.processed webhook path). The governed staff workflow in app/api/booking-operations/route.ts line 241 declares its state machine as {requested:["approved","rejected"],approved:["processing"],processing:["completed"]} and writes the terminal status 'completed' at line 247 - a value lib/unit-economics.ts never matches. lib/unit-economics.ts line 144 then documents the source as "booking_refund_cases status=processed", so the screen asserts the number is real.
money_consequence: Every refund settled by staff through the ops console rather than by a gateway webhook is invisible to the unit-economics ladder. Contribution margin, contribution % of GMV, revenue per provider-day and company contributionKnown are each overstated by the full refund amount - here Rs 5,000 on Rs 5,000 of GMV, i.e. the service was reported at 100% contribution margin when its true known contribution was 0. This is precisely a metric that drives a wrong commercial decision: a vertical with heavy manual refunds looks like the most profitable one on the board.
blast_radius: GET /api/unit-economics, all services and the company roll-up, every date window and every cityId filter. All verticals, because refund_requested/refund_status in app/api/booking-operations is the cross-vertical staff refund path.

title: P&L turnover and nett profit never subtract refunds - a booking refunded in full still reports Rs 5,000 revenue and Rs 5,000 nett profit for the month
actor: STAFF role_code=founder (f@pawspace.test); requires finance.view for GET /api/pnl-reporting
request:
Setup by the REAL governed refund workflow:
POST /api/booking-operations {"bookingId":"BKG-1","providerId":"PRV-1","action":"refund_requested","reason":"Groomer no-show, full refund"} -> 201
POST /api/booking-operations {"action":"refund_status","refundStatus":"approved"|"processing"|"completed",...} -> 200,200,200
Then: GET https://uat.pawspace.in/api/pnl-reporting?from=2026-08&to=2026-08 with headers {oai-authenticated-user-email: f@pawspace.test, oai-authenticated-user-full-name: Probe%20User, oai-authenticated-user-full-name-encoding: percent-encoded-utf-8}
response: 200. data.totalTurnover = {...,"2026-08":5000}; data.nettProfit = {...,"2026-08":5000}; data.revenue.subtotalAmount = 5000; data.totalExpensesAmount = 0. There is no refund, contra-revenue or cancellation line anywhere in the response - the report publishes Rs 5,000 of turnover and Rs 5,000 of profit for a month whose only transaction was refunded in full.
d1_after:
SELECT id,booking_id,amount,status FROM booking_refund_cases -> [{"id":"4b34df58-a9ce-4961-b7ef-56e47262eae7","booking_id":"BKG-1","amount":5000,"status":"completed"}]
SELECT * FROM booking_payments -> [{"id":"PAY-1","booking_id":"BKG-1","amount":5000,"status":"captured","method":"upi"}]
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM finance_journal_entries -> 0 (the refund posted no journal at all)
repeatable: yes - two independently built worlds in one process, both printed totalTurnover 2026-08 = 5000 and nettProfit 2026-08 = 5000 with a booking_refund_cases row at status='completed'
canonical_failure: lib/pnl-reporting.ts line 51: `const rows=await db.prepare("SELECT service_code,scheduled_start,total_amount FROM canonical_bookings WHERE status!='cancelled' AND status!='draft'").all<Row>();` - revenue is the gross booking amount and nothing is ever deducted from it. The only other input is the expense side at line 91, `SELECT account_code,entry_date,debit FROM finance_journal_entries WHERE posted=1 AND debit>0`, which is then matched against `expenseChartOfAccounts` (lib/chart-of-accounts.ts) whose account codes are all 6xxx - so even a posted contra-revenue journal could not appear. lib/finance-accounts.ts line 23 defines `REFUNDS: "4900-Refunds and Cancellations"` as contra-revenue, and a grep of lib/ and app/ shows that constant is referenced NOWHERE except its own definition: no code path ever posts a refund journal. Refunds are structurally absent from the P&L.
money_consequence: Turnover and nett profit are overstated by 100% of every refund the business issues. In the measured case a month with Rs 0 of retained revenue is published as Rs 5,000 turnover and Rs 5,000 profit. This is the statutory-style report a founder or an investor reads; it also feeds the monthly close, so a closed month freezes the overstated figure.
blast_radius: GET /api/pnl-reporting for every month and every vertical; and by extension the monthly close snapshot taken from the same computation. Every refund on the platform, all verticals - the gateway maps this route to finance.view.

title: Cash Flow Statement reports closing cash Rs 0 for a month in which Rs 5,000 was captured, because ordinary booking collections never post a journal
request: GET https://uat.pawspace.in/api/cash-flow-statement?period=2026-08 with headers {oai-authenticated-user-email: f@pawspace.test, oai-authenticated-user-full-name: Probe%20User, oai-authenticated-user-full-name-encoding: percent-encoded-utf-8}, run against a database holding one completed grooming booking of Rs 5,000 with a captured UPI payment of Rs 5,000 dated in the reported month.
response:
200 {"data":{"fromPeriod":"2026-08","toPeriod":"2026-08","method":"direct","openingCash":0,"closingCash":0,"netChangeInCash":0,"operating":{"total":0,"lines":[]},"investing":{"total":0,"lines":[]},"financing":{"total":0,"lines":[]},"reconciled":true,"detail":[]}}
Note `reconciled: true` - the statement asserts its own integrity while omitting every rupee the business actually collected.
d1_before: canonical_bookings: ('BKG-1',...,'completed',5000,...,'2026-08-10T09:00:00.000Z'); booking_payments: ('PAY-1','BKG-1',5000,'captured','upi'); finance_journal_entries: table created empty by ensureFinanceJournalTable
d1_after: unchanged. SELECT COUNT(*) FROM finance_journal_entries -> 0 both before and after the read; SELECT amount,status FROM booking_payments -> [{5000,'captured'}]. The cash exists in booking_payments and has no journal counterpart.
repeatable: yes - identical response on both passes of p03-pnl-refund.mjs against freshly built worlds
canonical_failure: lib/cash-flow-statement.ts line 34: `const rows=await db.prepare("SELECT id,source_type,account_code,debit,credit,narration,period_code FROM finance_journal_entries ORDER BY period_code,id").all<Row>().catch(()=>({results:[]}))` - the statement's ONLY input is finance_journal_entries, and cash movement is recognised only on lines whose account_code is in CASH_ACCOUNTS (lib/finance-accounts.ts line 26, {1000-Cash in Hand, 1010-Bank}). A grep for `postJournal(` across lib/ and app/ returns exactly four call sites: lib/pawspace-wallet-governance.ts:102 (wallet top-up), lib/pawspace-wallet-governance.ts:246 (wallet redeem, non-cash), lib/revenue-recognition-governance.ts:56 (only when recordDeferredRevenue is called with collectedToBank) and lib/revenue-recognition-governance.ts:82 (recognition, non-cash). No booking payment capture path - not app/api/canonical-bookings/route.ts:419, not app/api/grooming-payment-sandbox, not lib/grooming-payment-reconciliation.ts - ever calls postJournal. Absent journal is treated as no cash, and the `reconciled` flag at lib/cash-flow-statement.ts (openingCash+netMovement vs closingCash) is trivially satisfied by 0=0.
money_consequence: Operating cash inflow from the service business is structurally zero on the cash-flow statement. Closing cash, net change in cash and the operating section are each understated by the whole of collected service revenue. A finance user reading this alongside the P&L (which shows Rs 5,000 of turnover for the same month) sees a business that earned Rs 5,000 and banked nothing - the two published statements for one month cannot both be true.
blast_radius: GET /api/cash-flow-statement for every period and window. All verticals, since no vertical's payment capture posts a cash journal. Only wallet top-ups and explicitly-flagged deferred-revenue collections ever appear.

title: Company Analytics silently drops the whole final day of any explicit date window - GMV Rs 2,000 for a month that Unit Economics and the P&L both report as Rs 3,000
request:
Three completed grooming bookings of Rs 1,000 each on 2026-08-01, 2026-08-15 and 2026-08-31, then the same calendar month asked of three report surfaces with headers {oai-authenticated-user-email: f@pawspace.test, ...}:
GET https://uat.pawspace.in/api/company-analytics?from=2026-08-01&to=2026-08-31
GET https://uat.pawspace.in/api/unit-economics?from=2026-08-01&to=2026-08-31
GET https://uat.pawspace.in/api/pnl-reporting?from=2026-08&to=2026-08
d1_before: canonical_bookings (real DDL): BKG-A 2026-08-01T09:00:00.000Z completed 1000; BKG-B 2026-08-15T09:00:00.000Z completed 1000; BKG-C 2026-08-31T09:00:00.000Z completed 1000
d1_after: unchanged - SELECT id,scheduled_start,status,total_amount FROM canonical_bookings returns the same three rows after all three reads
repeatable: yes - two independently built worlds in one process both produced company-analytics gmv 2000 against unit-economics gmv 3000 and P&L turnover 3000
canonical_failure: lib/company-analytics.ts, buildCompanyAnalytics: `filters:string[]=["scheduled_start>=?","scheduled_start<?"]` with `binds=[from,to]`. scheduled_start is a full ISO timestamp ('2026-08-31T09:00:00.000Z') while `to` is a date-only string ('2026-08-31'), so the string comparison `'2026-08-31T09:00:00.000Z' < '2026-08-31'` is false and every booking on the closing date is excluded. app/api/company-analytics/route.ts passes url.searchParams.get("to") straight through with no normalisation. The sibling report lib/unit-economics.ts line 45 gets this right with `substr(scheduled_start,1,10)<=?`, which is why the two surfaces disagree.
money_consequence: Any caller that asks Company Analytics for a calendar month, week or quarter loses the last day of it. In the measured case that is a 33% understatement of GMV and of booking volume for the period, and it disagrees with Unit Economics and the P&L for the identical window - so month-end GMV, completion rate, cancellation rate, repeat rate, per-service margin and cost coverage are all computed on a short month. Month-end is exactly when the last day carries the highest volume.
blast_radius: GET /api/company-analytics whenever from/to are supplied (the route documents and accepts them). The two in-app consumers, app/team/analytics/page.tsx and app/control/business-intelligence-panel.tsx, currently call it with no window and so are unaffected - the exposure is API/report consumers that pass a window.

title: Launch Readiness handler enforces no permission at all and invents role 'associate' for an identity that has no app_users row - both gates disagree, only the gateway refuses
actor: (a) stranger@example.com - an identity with NO row in app_users; (b) cust@p.test - a provisioned identity whose role_code is 'customer'
request: GET https://uat.pawspace.in/api/launch-readiness with headers {oai-authenticated-user-email: <who>, oai-authenticated-user-full-name: Probe%20User, oai-authenticated-user-full-name-encoding: percent-encoded-utf-8}, plus the same request put through authorizeApiRequest(request,{DB}) to test gate 1 independently.
d1_before: app_users: exactly one row, ('U5','cust@p.test','C','customer','active'). No row for stranger@example.com. launch_readiness_items empty before the first call.
d1_after: launch_readiness_items seeded with the 12 system rows by ensureTables() - i.e. the unauthenticated-by-role caller's GET also performed the DDL and seed writes. app_users unchanged (SELECT email,role_code,status FROM app_users still returns only cust@p.test/customer/active - the handler does NOT persist the invented role).
repeatable: yes - identical on two consecutive passes
canonical_failure: app/api/launch-readiness/route.ts line 31, function actor(): `return {email,roleCode:email==="preview@pawspace.test"?"superuser":row?.role_code||"associate"}` - a missing app_users row falls through to the literal "associate" instead of refusing, and the GET at line 34 (`const a=await actor(request)`) then calls no requirePermission/authorize of any kind. Contrast lib/server-auth.ts resolveActor, which for the same input throws authFailure("Access has not been provisioned for this identity",403). Unknown identity is treated as satisfied, and unknown role is treated as staff.
money_consequence: No direct money movement (canWrite() still gates the POST on founder/superuser/admin/manager). The exposure is the platform's own launch posture: P0 gate statuses, evidence text, open critical operational exceptions, UAT sign-off records, the launch audit trail and the integration blocker list - the internal 'what is not ready' document. It is also a fail-open second gate: the whole refusal currently depends on worker/index.ts continuing to route this path through authorizeApiRequest.
blast_radius: GET /api/launch-readiness. Any identity header value at all, provisioned or not, reaches a 200 from the handler. Contained in production only by gate 1 (the gateway maps the route to launch.view).
